title: Quantitative Gaussian-Poisson Limits for a Target Contrast in a Finite-Information Treatment Cycle
banked_reason: Clean math and rubric reviews pass, but the delivered package is incremental: projected paper-score ceiling 6.2 is below 7.4, with no bounded in-scope salvage. Sharp first-order values concern the stipulated four-trial experiment; optimal calibration rates and useful finite-sample implementation remain open.
gap_reasons: The sharp first-order values concern a stipulated four-trial, binary-modifier triangular experiment; they do not establish a broadly applicable network-inference method. [Carter’s Theorem 1 and Lemma 2](https://carter.faculty.pstat.ucsb.edu/multi.pdf) supply the classical Gaussianization substrate, so the contribution must be assessed through the mixed decision problems and their original-data transfer; the disclosed internal manuscripts supply no independent novelty baseline. The reproduced edge-retention certificate establishes a scaled-MSE margin of only 0.0001540232558157017724 on one small parameter box, without strict honest-length gains or a finite-sample survival threshold. The quantitative upper and converse errors do not identify a sharp convergence rate or the first nonzero full-class oracle information price, and the framing correctly leaves those questions open rather than asserting a stale matched frontier. Certification establishes computable convergence, but the package supplies neither evaluated optimal honest-length values nor a demonstrated implementation at useful sample sizes, leaving its practical uncertainty benchmark incompletely developed. These substantive limits constrain the projected leading-econometrics-journal score despite the delivered first-order characterization clearing the field floor. proof_attempt_summary: Derived sharp first-order Gaussian plus labeled Poisson-sign decision values, data-only honest procedures, and a strict edge-retention risk certificate; final math and rubric panels passed without findings, with all three cited prerequisites verified. The delivered package fell below the field floor at the paper-score gate (6.2 < 7.4), with no bounded in-scope salvage; optimal calibration rates and useful finite-sample implementation remain open. No Lean formalization was attempted because the run terminated at D0.5.
tldr: This note studies quantitative inference for the target A--D causal contrast in a finite-information treatment cycle. Transported conditional edge contrasts arise from one feasible target mean vector, while source baseline risks range over lawful Bernoulli means in \([0,1]\) without an additional interiority restriction. Target means retain the stated \(\varepsilon\)-interiority condition. The established noisy Gaussian--Poisson approximation retains learned \(q,c\); the sharp first-order minimax values have same-class all-procedure converses and data-only attaining procedures with connected intervals of coverage at least \(9/10\) at every legal index. The attained excess is \(O_{\mathfrak s}(n^{-1/4}\log^2(1+n))\). An independent retained root certifies a strict asymptotic scaled-MSE gain from keeping each rare edge on \(\mathcal B\), with common margin at least \(0.0001540232558157017724\). The first nonzero full-class original-versus-oracle interval information price remains unresolved.
gap: The four-cycle manuscript \cite{InternalFourCycle} already supplies first-order minimax values, all-procedure transfer, and eventual honesty. Its deliberately conservative reserve and threshold do not determine the first nonzero finite-size decision cost. The published Gaussian and distribution-shift results inform the method but do not solve this coverage-constrained noisy-macro calibration question. Binary-treatment multi-source CATE transport motivates the setting; the network equation is an explicit primitive extension maintained here.
fill: The quantitative noisy-macro experiment and attained-excess ledger are the two root theorem targets. The fixed-box open question requires original-versus-oracle coverage-dual lower certificates or a demonstrable cancellation, then two-sided bounds on \(\mathcal Z_n\) and \(\mathcal T\). The \(n^{-1/4}\log^2 n\) ledger uses logarithmic Gaussian endpoint truncation instead of polynomial caps and replaces the banked \(n^{-1/128}\) reserve. Its sufficient attained-tolerance sample-size order is \(O_{\mathfrak s}(\zeta^{-4}\log^8(1/\zeta))\); a useful absolute frontier or edge-margin threshold also requires the open quantitative converse.
